analysis.title: Hedge Fund Trend Monitor: Bruised and broadening
key_insights: The report covers 1,001 hedge funds with $5.1 trillion of gross equity positions at the start of Q4 2026 ($3.3 trillion long, $1.9 trillion short), based on 13F filings as of September 30, 2026.

Hedge funds have struggled in the recent equity volatility. GS Prime Services estimates US equity long/short funds at +5% YTD through November 19, while the Hedge Fund VIP basket (GSTHHVIP) lagged the S&P 500, a basket of the most concentrated shorts, and the equal-weight S&P 500.

The VIP basket's 14 pp underperformance vs. the S&P 500 over the past six months matches its most significant underperformance vs. the market in its 20-year history. The basket has traded in line with GS's AI basket pair, with the strongest 3-month correlations to semiconductors and neoclouds.
Portfolio concentration and crowding are elevated. The median hedge fund holds 70% of its long book in its top 10 positions, and the GS Hedge Fund Crowding Index rose to a new record high in Q3.

Funds have cut leverage. Net leverage fell to the lowest level since Liberation Day (April 2025) and equity long/short net exposures now rival April 2025 as the lowest since pre-COVID. Gross leverage is well below its early-2026 peak but still elevated vs. the past few years.

Funds broadened their portfolios in Q3 by rotating incrementally away from AI. They cut TMT and added to cyclical and defensive sectors. Net tilts vs. the Russell 3000 rose most in Financials (+254 bp), Consumer Discretionary (+237 bp) and Industrials (+190 bp), with smaller adds to Consumer Staples (+154 bp) and Utilities (+120 bp). Info Tech tilt fell 619 bp.

Health Care is the largest net sector weight (19% of net exposure, +960 bp vs. the Russell 3000). Info Tech is the largest long weight (22%) but only 11% of net exposure, a large underweight vs. its 35% Russell 3000 weight. Tilts to Health Care, Financials, Consumer Discretionary, Utilities and Consumer Staples are at 10-year highs.
Factor exposure shifted from Growth toward Value, and Momentum exposure in long portfolios fell to its lowest since the AI trade began in early 2023.

Within mega-cap tech, funds added on net to META and NVDA and cut GOOGL. Net changes in owners were also negative for MSFT and AMZN in the AI-related decrease list. Hedge funds own about 5% of SPCX market cap, with 21 funds holding it as a top 10 position, so it enters the VIP basket.

INTC and META rank among the largest increases in hedge fund popularity (INTC for a second straight quarter, with 41 more owners). GOOGL and QCOM are Falling Stars. A majority of this quarter's Rising Stars are non-AI names, including ALL, HD, IQV and MRK.

Short interest across S&P 500 stocks has fallen in recent months but remains elevated. The median stock sits at 3.1% of market cap, in the 92nd percentile of 20 years. It is most elevated vs. history in defensive sectors, led by Utilities (99th percentile), Consumer Staples (95th) and Health Care (95th).

Largest recent increases in short interest as a share of float among Russell 1000 stocks over $5B include MDT (3% to 11%), AAL, TLN, IREN and CRWV. Largest decreases include SWKS, UTHR, IDA, MDLN and OLLI.

The VIP list holds the 50 stocks most often in funds' top 10 holdings. It has lagged the S&P 500 YTD (-3% vs. +6%) but outperformed in 58% of quarters since 2001, at the cost of high volatility. Info Tech is 28% of the basket. Fourteen new constituents entered, including AER, DHR, SGI, TOST, UNH and UNP. The basket rebalances after the close on November 24, 2026.

The High Concentration basket (GSTHHFHI, the 20 S&P 500 stocks with the highest hedge fund ownership of market cap) is +20% YTD, ahead of the S&P 500 by 14 pp. Six new constituents: CPT, FSLR, PCG, PNR, TKO and UHS.

ETF share of hedge fund long portfolios eased to 5.3% in Q3, near the highest since the GFC. ETF shorts of $314 billion are 64% of gross ETF exposure, while single-stock shorts are only 35% of gross single-stock positions. Funds use ETFs mainly as hedges.

Specialist funds concentrate in a few areas. Financials specialists favor regional banks, with the median listed stock owned by 27% of specialists vs. 1% of generalists. Health Care specialists favor biopharma, led by RVMD, INSM and ERAS.

The VISP basket (GSTHVISP) of 50 S&P 500 stocks with the largest dollar short interest is offered as a short hedge for the VIP long list. It excludes VIP names and stocks with more than 10% of float short. TSLA ($26.4B) and PLTR ($10.3B) lead.

GS argues 13F data is more reflective of current holdings than many assume, since 75% of stocks held on September 30, 2026 were also held on June 30, 2026. The analysis excludes derivatives, foreign holdings and offshore shorts.

trade_ideas.description: Short the GS VISP basket (GSTHVISP, equal-weighted 50 S&P 500 stocks with the largest dollar short interest, excluding VIP names and names with more than 10% of float short) as a hedge against a long position in the Hedge Fund VIP basket (GSTHHFVIP/GSTHHVIP)
trade_ideas.rationale: The VISP basket is designed as a short hedge for the Hedge Fund VIP List long portfolio.

risk_factors: Elevated portfolio concentration and crowding make it harder for fund managers when popular AI stocks sell off.
The VIP basket is highly correlated with the AI infrastructure trade, so further AI unwinds would hit hedge fund long books.
Momentum exposure is at its lowest since early 2023 and net leverage at its lowest since April 2025, which signals de-risking.
Short interest remains elevated vs. 20-year history across S&P 500 stocks, especially defensive sectors.
13F data has a 45-day delay, excludes derivatives, foreign holdings and offshore shorts, and may overstate portfolio density.
Rising Stars and concentration baskets are not sector-neutral, and the High Concentration basket skews to mid-caps.
charts_described: Exhibit 3 plots rolling 6-month excess return of Hedge Fund VIPs vs. the S&P 500: -14 pp in Nov '26, +10 pp in Jun '26, -15 pp in May '22, -13 pp in Dec '08 and +30 pp in Sep '20.
Exhibit 5 shows GS Prime Services leverage percentile ranks: overall net 70% (1-year 2%, 5-year 32%), overall gross 316% (89%, 98%), fundamental long/short net 42% (1%, 0%) and gross 205% (13%, 74%).
Exhibit 12 shows the weight of top 10 positions in the median hedge fund long portfolio at 70%, and Exhibit 13 shows the GS Hedge Fund Crowding Index rising in Q3.
Exhibit 17 shows SPCX owned by 108 funds in Q2 2026 (19 as a top 10 holding, 6% of equity cap) and 121 funds in Q3 2026 (21 top 10, 5%).

Exhibit 21 shows hedge fund net sector tilts vs. the Russell 3000: Health Care +960 bp, Industrials +517 bp, Financials +457 bp, Consumer Discretionary +437 bp, Comm Services -353 bp and Information Technology -2,384 bp.
vol_and_positioning: Net leverage for GS Prime Services equity long/short funds is 70% overall and 42% for the fundamental universe. Overall net sits in the 2nd percentile of the past year and 32nd of five years, while fundamental net is in the 1st percentile of the past year and 0th of five.
Gross leverage is 316% overall (89th percentile of the past year, 98th of five years) and 205% for the fundamental universe (13th and 74th percentiles).
Hedge fund crowding is at a record high and the top 10 positions are 70% of the median fund's long book.
Short interest for the median S&P 500 stock is 3.1% of market cap, and the 90th percentile stock is at 8%. The 20-year average for the median is 2.4%.

Short interest is most elevated vs. 20-year history in Utilities (3.5% vs. 2.0% average, 99th percentile), Consumer Staples (3.6% vs. 2.3%, 95th) and Health Care (2.6% vs. 2.0%, 95th). Energy is low at the 32nd percentile.
The highest short interest as a share of float among large Russell 1000 additions includes IREN at 26%, CRWV at 25%, WULF at 37% and AAL at 16%.

Among stocks over $25B, short interest as a percent of market cap is highest in NBIS (31%), LITE (14%), COIN (12%), LYV (11%), MCHP, HPQ, MRNA, MSTR, KHC, KMB, CNP, NKE, RKT, ON and AWK (about 8 to 9% each).
Among stocks under $1B, SOC has 95% of market cap short, followed by PCT (69%), ENVX (53%), DDD and XRX (50% each).

Hedge funds hold $489.8 billion gross in ETFs ($176.0 billion long, $313.8 billion short). The largest short positions are SPY ($63.5 billion), QQQ ($44.1 billion) and IWM ($21.4 billion), used as hedges.
The VISP short-hedge basket carries $283.2 billion of short interest across 50 S&P 500 names, with TSLA at $26.4 billion.

tension_points.bull_case: The VIP basket has outperformed the S&P 500 in 58% of quarters since 2001 with a 43 bp average quarterly excess return, and is a tool to follow the smart money from 13F filings.
tension_points.bear_case: The basket is tightly correlated with the AI trade, lagged the S&P 500 by 14 pp over six months (matching its worst on record), and crowding is at a record high.

theme_stances.key_argument: Elevated concentration and crowding have made it harder for managers as popular AI stocks sold off.
theme_stances.evidence: Elevated portfolio concentration and crowding have increased the challenge facing fund managers

theme_stances.theme: hedge fund rising and falling stars
theme_stances.key_argument: Stocks with the largest increase in hedge fund owners have historically outperformed sector peers in the following quarters, and Falling Stars have underperformed.
theme_stances.evidence: typically gone on to outperform sector peers during the quarters following their rise in popularity
